input_references.role: Timestamped points with matched-road coordinates, speed, context, and event attributes

metadata.goal: Identify the mobility patterns across weather and travel-mode conditions based on the given trajectories.
metadata.category: Weather, mode choice, distance, speed, and GPS alignment
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed WorldTrace case with 320 trajectories. Geometry source: Observed map-matched NYC WorldTrace road paths or continuous road-aligned return traversals. Environmental, temporal, mode, vehicle, and event attributes are arranged to make all stated comparisons measurable without changing the route coordinates used by the figures.

insight_list.question: How does the share of car trips differ under rainy, cold, and mild conditions?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Derive rainy and cold directly from native fields and compare the car share against mild conditions.
insight_list.code:
x=df.copy()
x['schema_condition']=np.select([x.weather.eq('rainy'),x.temperature_c.eq(5)&~x.weather.eq('rainy')],['rainy','cold'],default='mild')
order=['rainy','cold','mild'];tab=pd.crosstab(x.schema_condition,x.travel_mode,normalize='index').reindex(order)[['car','walking','cycling']]*100
print('Mode share (%)');print(tab.round(1))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5,4.8),constrained_layout=True)
tab.plot.bar(stacked=True,ax=ax,color=['#2563eb','#16a34a','#f59e0b'])
ax.set(title='Adverse conditions are more car-dominant',xlabel='condition',ylabel='share of trajectories (%)');ax.tick_params(axis='x',rotation=0);ax.legend(title='travel mode')
plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Walking trajectories recorded under mild weather and temperature conditions cover longer distances and show greater spatial extent, whereas walking during adverse weather remains more spatially compact and slower.

plot.title: Weather and Travel-Mode Mobility Patterns: Insight 2
plot.description: The map uses map-matched WorldTrace road geometry; the question-specific panel is computed from the same final CSV tables.

insight_list.question: What is the conditional walking pattern P(speed | weather, temperature), and how do distance and spatial extent differ between adverse and mild conditions?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use every weather-temperature cell specified in the YAML, then compare walking distance and per-trajectory endpoint displacement between adverse and mild conditions.
insight_list.code:
w=df[df.travel_mode.eq('walking')].copy();w['speed_mps']=w.mean_speed_kmh/3.6
conditional=w.groupby(['weather','temperature_c']).agg(trips=('trajectory_id','size'),speed_mps=('speed_mps','mean'),speed_sd=('speed_mps','std'),distance_km=('trajectory_distance_km','mean'))
print('P(speed | weather, temperature) summary');print(conditional.round(3))
w['weather_group']=np.where(w.condition_group.str.startswith('adverse'),'adverse','mild')
print('Adverse/mild trajectory-extent summary');print(w.groupby('weather_group').agg(trips=('trajectory_id','size'),distance_km=('trajectory_distance_km','mean'),endpoint_displacement_km=('straight_line_distance_km','mean')).round(3))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(15,4.8),constrained_layout=True)
colors={'rainy':'#2563eb','cloudy':'#64748b','sunny':'#f59e0b'}
for weather,color in colors.items():
    q=conditional.xs(weather,level='weather');ax[0].errorbar(q.index,q.speed_mps,yerr=q.speed_sd.fillna(0),marker='o',capsize=3,label=weather,color=color)
ax[0].set(title='Conditional walking speed',xlabel='temperature (°C)',ylabel='walking speed (m/s)');ax[0].legend(title='weather');ax[0].grid(alpha=.25)
groups=[w[w.weather_group.eq(k)].trajectory_distance_km for k in ['adverse','mild']]
parts=ax[1].violinplot(groups,showmeans=True,showmedians=True);ax[1].set_xticks([1,2],['adverse','mild']);ax[1].set(title='Walking-distance distributions',xlabel='condition',ylabel='trajectory distance (km)');ax[1].grid(axis='y',alpha=.25)
for group,color in [('adverse','#2563eb'),('mild','#f59e0b')]:
    q=w[w.weather_group.eq(group)];ax[2].scatter(q.trajectory_distance_km,q.straight_line_distance_km,s=26,alpha=.6,label=group,color=color)
ax[2].set(title='Per-trajectory walking spatial extent',xlabel='trajectory distance (km)',ylabel='start-to-end displacement (km)');ax[2].legend();ax[2].grid(alpha=.2)
plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Among car trips, adverse-weather trajectories show lower speeds and greater point-to-road offsets for GPS data in highly turning sections, while dry-weather trajectories maintain more stable speeds and closer road alignment

insight_list.question: Among car trips, how do speed level, speed stability, and GPS-to-road alignment vary with adverse weather, especially in highly turning sections?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare adverse and mild/dry car speed statistics, then show the interaction between weather condition and high-turn road segments for GPS-road offset.
insight_list.code:
c=df[df.travel_mode.eq('car')].copy();c['weather_group']=np.where(c.condition_group.str.startswith('adverse'),'adverse','mild/dry')
g=c.groupby('weather_group').agg(mean_speed=('mean_speed_kmh','mean'),within_speed_sd=('within_trip_speed_sd_kmh','mean'),mean_offset=('mean_gps_road_offset_m','mean')).reindex(['adverse','mild/dry'])
q=user_df[user_df.travel_mode.eq('car')].copy();q['weather_group']=np.where(q.condition_group.str.startswith('adverse'),'adverse','mild/dry')
h=q.groupby(['weather_group','is_high_turn_segment']).distance_to_matched_road_m.agg(['mean','std','count'])
print('Car trajectory summary');print(g.round(2));print('GPS-road offset by weather and turning section');print(h.round(2))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.8),constrained_layout=True)
pos=np.arange(len(g));ax[0].plot(pos,g.mean_speed,marker='o',linewidth=2,label='mean speed');ax[0].plot(pos,g.within_speed_sd,marker='s',linewidth=2,label='within-trip speed SD')
ax[0].set_xticks(pos,g.index);ax[0].set(title='Car speed level and stability',xlabel='weather condition',ylabel='speed metric (km/h)');ax[0].legend();ax[0].grid(alpha=.25)
for group,color in [('adverse','#dc2626'),('mild/dry','#16a34a')]:
    z=h.loc[group];ax[1].errorbar([0,1],z['mean'],yerr=z['std'],marker='o',capsize=3,label=group,color=color)
ax[1].set_xticks([0,1],['ordinary section','high-turn section']);ax[1].set(title='GPS-road offset increases at adverse high-turn sections',xlabel='road section type',ylabel='point-to-road offset (m)');ax[1].legend();ax[1].grid(alpha=.25)
plt.show()
